signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: CAD/JPY momentum accelerates as the G10 scorecard flags a critical bilateral theme with a 1.634% spread. CAD leads G10 performance with a +0.816% average, supported by a positive ESI of +11.6 and a 125bp OIS carry advantage over JPY. JPY remains the G10 laggard at -0.818%, pressured by a -0.70% real policy rate and a bull flattener yield curve regime that favors carry seekers. USD/JPY holding at 159.55 remains below its SMA20/50 cluster (160.79/161.13), keeping JPY under broad technical pressure despite a Strong Positive ESI of +16.3. The 275bp BoE-BoJ and 335bp RBA-BoJ spreads reinforce the JPY-short theme across the complex. Trade bias: Bearish JPY; CAD outperformance and carry differentials drive the bilateral divergence. Catalyst: BoC meeting 9 Sep — 100% hold priced. Risk: Sharp risk-off sentiment spike triggers JPY safe-haven flows and compresses the scorecard spread below 0.80%.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Positioning + Volatility + Macro Sentiment
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3486, holding firmly above its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 1.3369-1.3423. Standard Chartered reports resilient UK GDP growth, supporting the BoE's hold stance at 3.75% while US PPI at 4.7% y/y underwhelms hawkish Fed bets. COT LF net long sits at +39,039 (70.1% long), marking a crowded institutional stance as the pair tests monthly highs. Options markets are pricing significant protection with a +5.0% Vol Risk Premium (IV 11.0% vs HV30 6.0%), suggesting traders are hedging for a breakout rather than complacent positioning. Retail sentiment remains a contrarian tailwind with 67% of retail traders short. Trade bias: Bullish GBP/USD; resilient UK macro and soft US inflation data support the trend above SMA clusters. Catalyst: US CPI next week. Risk: UK growth data disappoints, prompting a rapid unwind of the 70.1% spec long position.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew vs Realized Vol Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY at 159.55 exhibits a significant divergence between options pricing and realized volatility. The 25d Risk Reversal at -2.07 indicates a strong institutional bias for JPY calls (USD/JPY puts), pricing in aggressive protection against a downside move or BoJ intervention. Despite this, the Vol Risk Premium is negative at -1.6% (IV 7.2% vs HV30 8.8%), revealing unusual complacency in realized vol terms. JPY COT LF net short remains extreme at -63,633, suggesting the pair is vulnerable to a squeeze if US yields continue to soften. JPY's mildly accommodative real rate of -0.70% keeps the carry trade structurally intact for now while VIX at 14.6 limits safe-haven demand. Trade bias: Neutral/Range USD/JPY; strong downside options skew offsets the 275bp carry advantage. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 57% hike priced). Risk: A sustained break above 160.00 triggers verbal or physical BoJ intervention, validating the aggressive RR skew.

signals.title: NZD/USD — ESI Outperformance + Positioning Squeeze
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5852, supported by a Strong Positive ESI of +15.8, indicating New Zealand data is consistently outperforming expectations. The RBNZ remains the most hawkish G10 central bank, currently hiking with a 2.5% policy rate, yet COT LF positioning shows an extreme net short of -30,785 (long% only 9.7%). This institutional crowd-short contradicts the positive data trend and the RBNZ's hiking cycle, creating a high-conviction short-squeeze setup. Price remains above the SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.5788-0.5846), confirming a bullish technical posture. While NZD faces a -125bp OIS carry disadvantage vs USD, the negative real rate of -1.56% is improving as inflation expectations stabilize. Trade bias: Bullish NZD/USD; extreme spec short positioning faces a data-led squeeze. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep — Hike bias priced. Risk: RBNZ shifts to a surprise hold, validating the large spec short position.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Volatility Premium + Cross-Asset Correlation Break
signals.text: EUR/USD at 1.1531 is trading with an elevated vol premium (VRP +2.9%), as IV at 7.1% remains significantly above the realized HV30 of 4.2%. Institutional demand for hedging is high despite a relatively calm spot market and a neutral retail bias (57% short). A notable correlation break is active where EUR/USD vs EuroStoxx (z=+1.94σ) deviates from the historical norm, suggesting EUR is decoupling from regional equity performance. ECB's hike bias and a mildly restrictive real rate of +0.09% provide support against the USD's 135bp carry advantage. Technically, the pair is positioned above its SMA20 (1.1474) and SMA50 (1.147), but remains capped by the SMA200 at 1.1634. Trade bias: Neutral EUR/USD; high vol premium and correlation instability suggest consolidation. Catalyst: ECB meeting 10 Sep — Hike bias priced. Risk: US 10Y yields break higher, reasserting the USD carry advantage and pressuring the 1.147 support cluster.
